news_analysis.headline_hook: Repo rate 25 bps hike: How your home loan math changes overnight
news_analysis.breaking_event_summary: The Reserve Bank of India raised the repo rate by 25 bps to 5.50% after nearly three years, while upgrading the national GDP forecast by 40 bps to 7.1%.
news_analysis.retail_illusion: Borrowers may assume home loan interest rates will remain unchanged due to a strong economic GDP growth outlook.
news_analysis.institutional_reality: A repo rate hike increases the cost of funds for commercial banks, which directly leads to an upward revision in floating loan rates and higher monthly EMIs for retail borrowers.
news_analysis.actionable_retail_rule: Review your home loan reset clause and check if your interest rate is linked to the External Benchmark Lending Rate (EBLR) to anticipate EMI or tenure changes.
news_analysis.editorial_directive: Use crisp, punchy Tanglish. Avoid formal Tamil terms like 'vattividham' where 'interest rate' is understood. Focus on the direct impact: 'EMI math' and 'loan tenure'. Ensure the tone remains professional yet urgent, emphasizing that policy changes aren't just headlines, but adjustments to the user's monthly budget.

stat_data.label: GDP Forecast
stat_data.context: India-voda GDP forecast 40 bps increase aagi 7.1%-ah iruku. Economic growth nalla irundhalum, inflation-ah control panna RBI repo rate-ah hike pannirukanga.

slides.title: Repo Rate Hike: The Reality
slides.card_text: Repo rate 5.50%-ku uyarthirukanga. Idhu bank-ku funds borrow panna cost-ah increase pannum. So, banks unga floating interest rate-ah upward revision panna chance iruku.

comparison_data.myth: Strong GDP growth irundha, interest rate change aagathu.
comparison_data.reality: GDP growth-um inflation-um balance panna RBI repo rate-ah hike pannuvanga, idhu direct-ah unga EMI-ah affect pannum.
